question: Do an e-Sanad apostille and an e-Cinepramaan film application certify the same thing?

- e-Sanad is MEA’s platform for verification, attestation and apostille of personal, educational and commercial documents issued in India [11_Defence_and_Foreign_Affairs.txt#page-2-chunk-9].  
- An apostille issued via MEA authenticates the signature or seal and the capacity of the signatory; it does not certify the content of the underlying document. Verification by the document‑issuing authority must precede MEA attestation/apostille. Uploading a document, issuer verification, and apostille issuance are distinct stages [11_Defence_and_Foreign_Affairs.txt#page-2-chunk-11].  
- Reporting guidance warns not to equate an apostille with a foreign institution’s acceptance of a qualification, job offer or visa — those are separate matters [11_Defence_and_Foreign_Affairs.txt#page-2-chunk-12].

- e-Cinepramaan is the Central Board of Film Certification’s online route for submitting film‑certification applications, paying fees, checking status and responding to observations [14_Science_IT_and_Communication.txt#page-3-chunk-10].

- An e-Sanad apostille attests to the authenticity of signatures/seals and the signatory’s capacity on documents; an e-Cinepramaan application is the process for obtaining a CBFC film‑certification decision. They are different kinds of certification and do not certify the same thing [11_Defence_and_Foreign_Affairs.txt#page-2-chunk-11] [14_Science_IT_and_Communication.txt#page-3-chunk-10].
